extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in mathematics and math communicators (popularizers/writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing explanatory/popular-mathematics pieces for a lay or broadly literate audience that convey the aesthetic of mathematical elegance. Emphasizes choices communicators should make to produce text that feels 'elegant' to non-specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness with depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics 'condenses verbose conversations, sprawling across multiple pages, into a few concise lines of equations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor economy: present ideas in tight, concentrated form that nonetheless carry substantial conceptual weight. Examples/anti-patterns: good — a compact formula that summarizes a long argument; bad — long-winded prose that fails to reveal the underlying simplicity or content. Aim for conveying deep content in minimal, memorable expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encapsulation of truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics holds 'the axioms, context, and the very essence of logic and truth,' not merely symbols and numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize that mathematical statements encode underlying assumptions and logical structure. In exposition, make clear the conceptual core or 'truth' the equations capture rather than treating symbols as opaque. Avoid presenting formulas without explaining the axioms/context that give them meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal connectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Elegant equations unite disparate fields (example: 'Euler's identity = exponential + imaginary unit + fundamental constants').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight connections across areas — show how a single relation links multiple domains or concepts. Use iconic examples (Euler's identity) to illustrate how compact expressions synthesize diverse mathematical notions. Anti-pattern: siloed presentation that hides cross-disciplinary relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridging abstract and concrete
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics connects theoretical concepts to observable phenomena (example: 'Maxwell's equations predicting electromagnetic waves and light').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing for lay audiences, explicitly draw lines between abstract formalism and physical or tangible examples. Use historical or scientific instances where mathematical ideas predicted or explained real phenomena to make the abstract concrete. Avoid purely formal discussion that fails to show real-world impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revealing hidden structures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on exposition that uncovers unexpected patterns, symmetries, or structures beneath apparent complexity. Use illustrative examples that make the hidden structure visible (diagrams, metaphors, simple special cases). Anti-pattern: presenting results as isolated facts without showing the organizing principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity reflecting complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Elegance emerges when 'profound simplicity' underlies 'apparent complexity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey how simple principles can generate complex behavior; show derivations or conceptual reductions that reduce complexity to a small set of ideas. Emphasize conceptual economy rather than just surface simplicity. Avoid oversimplification that strips essential content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lay-audience math writing preferences (economy, universality, bridges, revelation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implication: Lay-audience math writing favors: economy + universality + bridge-to-physics + hidden-structure-revelation. These differ from researcher-internal aesthetics (e.g., 'rigor' or 'non-emulation of Knuth').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When crafting popular math pieces, prioritize concise, universal, and concrete-bridging presentations that reveal structure. Recognize that academic priorities (rigor, exhaustive generality, stylistic norms of specialists) may not map onto what a lay audience finds elegant. Adjust tone, explanation, and example selection accordingly.
